label: late original-phase input of k/a/t/r/y/o/m
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never on t<=3, the delimiter, or the copy phase. Rate rises steeply with position (orig_idx 4: 0.7%, 6: 6%, 7: 13%, 8: 19%), so it fires mostly on the last one or two original tokens of long sequences (L=8-9 hold ~87% of mass). It is strongly token-selective: k, a, t, r (about 4-5x lift), then y, o, m, with weaker w, j, e; g and digits almost never. It prefers first occurrences of the token (in_first lift 1.5x). The first original token modulates it in a graded way (l, q, w, v, i, g, d, b raise the rate about 2x), and many predicted steps stay below threshold. This looks like an additive mix of position, token, and context, not a crisp rule. The predicate (t>=6 plus token set) gets dev F1 0.48, mass recall 0.78.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: k, a, t, r, y, o; least: f, q, 3, 1) and the first original token (most: q, l, w, g, v, i; least: r, k, j, p); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, t=7, t=6.
